nodes.label: Cross-database LGPD erasure & portability design doc
LGPD erasure & portability across three databases
nodes.rationale: Three services own separate Postgres databases with no cross-database FK, cascade, or two-phase commit; honoring erasure/export means one logical operation across all three. brain-api, as the only service with a 'who is asking' concept, orchestrates over each service's own internal HTTP surface — it never reaches into another DB. It also never assumes what 'erased' means elsewhere: precheck may anonymize rather than hard-delete clinical records it must legally retain (CFM retention rules).

nodes.label: Idempotent retry-as-resume semantics
nodes.rationale: The whole flow is idempotent: re-running an erasure re-executes deletes that match zero rows and upstream calls that report zero counts. partial (still 200, never an error) means the caller retries the same request — a retry only re-touches what a prior partial run did not reach; there is no separate resume endpoint because the retry IS the resume.

nodes.label: Identifiers-only-as-sha256 audit rule
nodes.rationale: subject_hash is computed from the normalized subject key BEFORE any deletion and is the only reference to the subject ever persisted; the raw email/wa_id is never written, logged, or included in result. Export bundles are reduced to counts before the audit write — the response carries the full bundle (the point of an export), the audit row never does. structlog redaction is defense-in-depth, not the primary guarantee.
